transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... I just can't seem to shake this heavy feeling lately. It's this constant mix of fear and guilt. I'm just tense all day, honestly, like I'm just waiting for something else to go wrong. And... I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened. It's just always there.
Do you find yourself having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened?

Yeah, I do. Mostly it's the memories. I'm a building inspector, so I'm on work sites a lot, and... well, I'll just be measuring a railing, or maybe I'll hear a ladder scrape against a wall, and out of nowhere I can see my husband falling. 

It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops completely, and my hands get really shaky. So, yes, they definitely pop up when I don't want them to.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
It's been going on for about four months now. Basically ever since my husband's fall, when we were doing that porch repair. That's when all this started.
Have you been trying to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the fall?

Yeah, I have. At work, I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. I just pass them on to someone else. And at home... well, I find excuses not to talk about the repair we were doing. I even avoid looking out at the spot in the yard where it actually happened. I just try to steer clear of all of it as much as I can.

latest_inference.note: Patient clearly meets DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1): exposure to a traumatic event (witnessing husband's fall), intrusive symptoms (flashbacks/vivid memories with physiological reactivity), avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (avoiding decks/porches, work, the yard, discussing the event), negative cognitions/mood (pervasive guilt, self-blame, persistent fear), and marked hyperarousal (tense all day, awaiting catastrophe), lasting 4 months (>1 month) with functional impairment. Adjustment disorder (F43.2) and major depressive episode (F32) are ruled out.
